content.title: Nuggets vs. Spurs: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (3/12/26)
content.text: The Denver Nuggets (40–26) face the San Antonio Spurs (48–17) tonight at Frost Bank Center. Denver enters after a 128–93 win over the Houston Rockets last night, rebounding from back-to-back losses to the New York Knicks and Oklahoma City Thunder with a dominant two-way performance. Jamal Murray led with 30 points on 11-of-21 shooting, and Nikola Jokic posted his 25th triple-double of the season. Christian Braun scored 19, Cam Johnson added 17, and Tim Hardaway Jr. finished with 14 off the bench, most of that coming from four 3-pointers. Denver led for nearly the entire game, holding the Rockets to under 95 points with heavy defensive pressure, including 12 steals. San Antonio, meanwhile, has won five straight and nine out of its last 10 games, beating some of the league’s top teams along the way. On Tuesday, the Spurs defeated the Boston Celtics, 125–116, at home after routing the Rockets by 25. Victor Wembanyama was on fire from deep, tying a career-high eight 3-pointers and finishing with 39 points on the night. De’Aaron Fox put the best version of himself on the court, scoring 25 on 11-of-14 shooting. And Stephon Castle added 18 points. The Spurs are locked in what is effectively a two-team race with the Thunder for the top spot in the West, trailing OKC by just 2.5 games. The third-place Rockets are 10.5 games out. The Spurs have a slight edge here at home, but this game could go either way, given the seemingly limitless ceiling for the Jokic-Murray tandem. Final Score Prediction: San Antonio Spurs 121, Denver Nuggets 117 Injury Report Denver Nuggets Jamal Murray — GTD (Ankle) Aaron Gordon — GTD (Hamstring) Peyton Watson — Out (Hamstring) San Antonio Spurs Victor Wembanyama — GTD (Ankle) Lindy Waters III — GTD (Illness) Harrison Barnes — GTD (Ankle) David Jones-Garcia — OFS (Ankle) How to Watch Nuggets vs. Spurs Tip-off for tonight’s Nuggets-Spurs game is set for 9:00 PM Eastern / 8:00 PM Central / 7:00 PM Mountain at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio. The game airs live locally on Altitude Sports and FanDuel Sports Network Southwest. Out-of-market viewers can stream the matchup on NBA League Pass for free on Amazon Prime Video with a 7-day free trial here. Amazon also offers a discounted subscription that starts at $12.74 for the first two months (then $16.99/month). The subscription also includes access to NBA TV. Fans can also choose a Team Pass to follow one team’s games for $13.99 per month.
